_: Placements Innes has decided by eye. The checker measures detail; it cannot
see a SUBJECT, and it does not know that a character outranks a building.
Anything listed here is his call, and apply-placement.py will not touch it -
not now, and not the next time someone runs the checker over the line.
'why' is his own wording wherever there is any.
AN ABSENT DECK MEANS NEVER REVIEWED. It does NOT mean reviewed and clean.
Five decks have no entry at all: past-simple-2, present-simple-2,
present-continuous-2, future-simple-2, and (until now) past-simple. Do not
let apply-placement.py run unsupervised on those.
PIN EVERY SLIDE HE NAMES, WHICHEVER WAY THE MEASUREMENT FALLS. The earlier
rule was to pin only where he OVERRULED the measurement, and that rule lost
three of his instructions on Past Simple: 7, 16 and 19 scored x1.12, x1.02
and x1.11, all under the x1.30 threshold, so apply-placement left them and
nothing recorded that he had asked. They sat where he objected to them.
A pin is the record of the instruction, not only of the disagreement.
